answer: An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Because a fabricated citation fails the wander check immediately, the horizon audit keeps the resolved set and the inlet replay makes public exactly which ids were live. Copying the same citations across 73 aliases therefore burns the reading cost 73 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 23 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
